newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks close firm on foreign bids.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks close firm on foreign bids.

text.p: Caracas stocks recouped morning losses as afternoon foreign bidding re-floated blue chips that were dented Wednesday and early Thursday by profit-taking, traders said.
"Shares regained their level on foreign buying, especially in Electricidad de Caracas," said Cavelba broker Eduardo Blanco.
The market's 19-share index closed ahead 0.24 percent at 4,862.03 points as ten million shares traded to a total value of 2 billion bolivars ($425 million).

Bellwether stock Electricidad gained 2.00 bolivars to close at 428.00 as investors continued to speculate on possible electricity tariff rate rises. Among traded issues, 20 rose, 11 fell and nine closed flat.
"Buyers are keeping the market afloat," said another broker.
On Wednesday, profit-taking interrupted the stock market's three day string of consecutive highs that was spurred by gaining confidence in Venezuela's economic prospects.
